name_note: GTDB splits the classical genus Coprococcus, and g__Coprococcus_A holds Coprococcus catus and Coprococcus_A intestinihominis rather than all Coprococcus species.

sentences.text: Coprococcus catus is an intestinal bacterium that uses lactate, converting it to short-chain fatty acids including butyrate in the human gut.
A study that mined genomes of lactate utilizers for genes involved in propionate formation reported a propanediol utilization compartment annotated in Coprococcus catus.
A comparative metagenomics study of nine Crohn's disease patients and nine healthy controls reported Coprococcus catus-like species at significantly lower abundance in the patients.
In infant gut metagenomes from the first year of life, horizontal gene transfer in vaginally delivered infants was reported to be driven primarily by Coprococcus catus.
